speaker: Patient
text: 5-day-old male newborn. The newborn's mother reports that her child has developed yellowish discoloration of the skin that started from the face and then spread to the trunk since the past day. There have been no changes in his bowel habits or urination. The baby was born full-term at 38 weeks’ gestation via an uncomplicated vaginal delivery and has been exclusively breastfed every 2–3 hours.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the history; the progression from face to trunk in a 5-day-old exclusively breastfed infant with normal bilirubin levels is highly suggestive of breastfeeding jaundice. To rule out other causes, I need to see if the stool color has changed to pale or clay-colored, which would indicate biliary obstruction. REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal_Ultrasound

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Breastfeeding Jaundice (Physiologic Jaundice). The clinical presentation of a 5-day-old exclusively breastfed infant with jaundice spreading from face to trunk and normal liver function tests (bilirubin 7 mg/dL, direct 0.6 mg/dL) is classic for this condition. No further imaging is required.
